domain_label: Multimodal Capture & Voice Answering (code voice) — record → queue → nightly transcribe → LLM rubric-grade → learner-model write-back
purpose: A method for turning spoken exam answers in any language into rubric-graded learning signal through an asynchronous, single-user pipeline: capture per-answer audio, store it plus a metadata row and enqueue it in SQLite, drain the queue nightly through a transcriber INTERFACE with interchangeable local (whisper.cpp / faster-whisper) and cloud (Google/Azure/Amazon/OpenAI) implementations, LLM-grade each transcript against the exam rubric — a practice ETS SpeechRater precedent shows is established for spoken answers — and write the grade back to the learner model, keeping local-vs-cloud a config flag rather than a rewrite and tagging every design-synthesis claim as an estimate and every vendor/regulatory claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN at the fetch grade the research supports.
assumptions: no live benchmark of this exact pipeline is supplied; every score is a heuristic prior, and every architecture claim (the async queue, the interface seam, the nightly worker, the write-back path) is design synthesis tagged ESTIMATE, distinct from the vendor/library facts it is built on
the system is single-user: a directory of audio files plus one SQLite table is sufficient and a message broker is overkill, so scale-out concerns are deliberately out of band
the owner explicitly DEFERRED the local-vs-cloud transcription choice, so the binding requirement is that both paths stay open behind one interface, not that either is selected now
nightly batch analysis has no real-time latency constraint, so even CPU-only whisper.cpp medium/large is adequate and GPU/cloud speed is a convenience, not a requirement

Whisper's own language-identification handles the owner's 'whatever language' requirement without asking the learner to declare a language, but per-language accuracy varies and is not uniform across the 100 codes
exclusions: the gamification / visual-progress calendar, streak mechanics and the goal-gradient/habit psychology in Part A of the research file belong to the engagement/UX specialist and are not modelled here
the flashcard-quality and book-decomposition rules that the voice-note post-processing hands off to (flashcards_and_book_decomposition.md) are named as a downstream consumer, not specified here
the scheduler/SRS that consumes the learner-model update next morning is named as the write-back consumer but its internals (interval math, backlog view) belong to the scheduling specialist

delivery/pronunciation scoring (fluency, pause patterns) is scoped OUT of the default content grader and held as a future audio-path step, quantified only where TOEFL-speaking makes delivery part of the construct

stating an exact current cloud-STT language count, an exact ETS human/machine score weighting, or a specific non-OpenAI vendor's current retention terms as fact — each is held UNKNOWN pending a live fetch

competency_questions.question: What did the owner actually require for voice answering, and which parts are binding vs deferred?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OWNER_CAPTURE_BRIEF states the ~10-spoken-answers-in-any-language, saved-and-queued-for-later-AI-analysis requirement plus voice note-making, and marks local-vs-cloud as an owner-DEFERRED decision the architecture must keep open, tagged FACT to the owner brief

competency_questions.question: Why is an asynchronous record-now/analyse-later pipeline the right posture, and how does the queue state machine encode it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASYNC_PIPELINE_POSTURE justifies no-real-time-ASR / nightly batch aligned with the owner's every-night analysis, and QUEUE_STATE_MACHINE gives the queued→transcribed→graded|failed(reason) lifecycle with nothing silently dropped, both tagged ESTIMATE-design

competency_questions.question: How does the transcriber interface seam keep the deferred local-vs-cloud choice a config flag instead of a rewrite?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRANSCRIBER_INTERFACE_SEAM defines one interface with LocalWhisper and CloudSTT implementations so the decision is a config flag, and both implementations are named with their grounding

competency_questions.question: How is each spoken answer captured and durably stored/enqueued, and why is SQLite-plus-files sufficient?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUDIO_CAPTURE_RECORD specifies one 16 kHz mono file per answer and STORE_ENQUEUE_SQLITE writes the file plus a metadata row {answer_id,question_id,session_id,recorded_at,duration,language_hint?,status} and argues a broker is overkill at single-user scale

competency_questions.question: What is the queue lifecycle and how are failures handled without silent loss?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUEUE_STATE_MACHINE and FAILURE_RETRY_HANDLING define the statuses, the failed(reason) capture, the next-night retry, and the rule that nothing is silently dropped

competency_questions.question: How is the owner's 'whatever language' requirement met, and what is the real coverage and accuracy caveat?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LANGUAGE_COVERAGE states Whisper's LANGUAGES dict is exactly 100 entries [FACT — fetched/counted], that language-identification removes the need for the learner to declare a language, that detected-language+confidence is stored, and that per-language accuracy varies

competency_questions.question: What does the nightly batch-transcribe worker do and what does it produce?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BATCH_TRANSCRIBE_WORKER drains status=queued through the interface, produces a transcript plus detected language+confidence, advances status to transcribed, and has no latency constraint so CPU-only local models suffice

competency_questions.question: How is a transcript rubric-graded, and why is automated grading of spoken answers not exotic?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RUBRIC_GRADE_LLM feeds transcript + the question's model answer/rubric to an LLM grader emitting {score, per-dimension subscores, error notes, misconception tags}, and SPEECHRATER_PRECEDENT grounds it in ETS SpeechRater (operating since ~2008, TOEFL iBT Speaking scored human+machine) with the exact weighting held UNKNOWN

competency_questions.question: Should the grader score content or delivery, and where does delivery live?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTENT_VS_DELIVERY_SCORING grades CONTENT from the transcript by default, carves out TOEFL-speaking where delivery is part of the construct, and keeps the audio path available because fluency/pause features live in the audio not the transcript

competency_questions.question: How does a grade update the learner model, and how is the decision kept auditable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEARNER_MODEL_WRITEBACK updates per-item mastery + weakness map for the next-morning scheduler, and AUDIT_LINKAGE keeps audio+transcript+grade linked (with Whisper word timestamps) to answer 'why did it say I was wrong?'

competency_questions.question: What are the privacy and vendor-retention considerations for cloud audio, and what is the default posture?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRIVACY_CLOUD_AUDIO cites EDPB Guidelines 02/2021 (voice personal; Article 9 biometric only when processed to identify) and the never-run-speaker-ID rule, VENDOR_DATA_RETENTION cites OpenAI's not-trained-by-default/≤30-day terms with other vendors UNKNOWN, and LOCAL_DEFAULT_RECOMMENDATION defaults to local with cloud as one adapter swap plus consent

competency_questions.question: How does the voice-note path reuse the pipeline, and what is the pipeline go/no-go verdict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VOICE_NOTE_PIPELINE reuses record→transcribe→LLM-post-process→human-confirm minus grading, and PIPELINE_GO_NOGO composes the per-stage gates (durable queue, language coverage, SpeechRater-grounded grading, auditable write-back, local-default privacy) into a defensible verdict

glossary.definition: The record-now / analyse-later design [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4]: capture writes audio + a queued metadata row and returns immediately; a nightly worker does the slow transcription and grading. No real-time ASR is needed, which is the cheap and robust choice for a single-user study system.

One abstract TranscriberInterface with two concrete implementations — LocalWhisper (whisper.cpp / faster-whisper) and CloudSTT — so the owner's DEFERRED local-vs-cloud choice becomes a config flag, not a rewrite. The seam is the architectural answer to 'the local AI or the cloud, later on decision.'

Whisper's built-in detection of the spoken language, which lets the system honour 'whatever language' without asking the learner to declare one; the detected language and its confidence are stored on the row. Whisper's LANGUAGES table has exactly 100 entries [FACT — fetched and counted from openai/whisper tokenizer.py].

The status lifecycle on each answer row: queued → transcribed → graded, or → failed(reason) on any stage error; failed items retry the next night and nothing is silently dropped. This is the durability contract of the pipeline [ESTIMATE — design].

The LLM step that takes the transcript plus the question's model answer / rubric and returns {score, per-rubric-dimension subscores, error notes, misconception tags}. It grades the CONTENT of the answer, not pronunciation, unless the course is TOEFL-speaking where delivery is part of the construct.

ETS's automated engine for scoring spontaneous non-native speech, operating since ~2008; operational TOEFL iBT Speaking is scored by a combination of human raters and SpeechRater [FACT — via search snippets; ets.org direct fetch 403]. It establishes that machine-grading spoken answers against a rubric is normal practice; the exact current human/machine weighting is [UNKNOWN].

The step where the grade updates the per-item mastery state and weakness map that the next-morning scheduler consumes; the day-view effort metric and the course-view mastery metric are different and must not be conflated.

Keeping audio + transcript + grade linked so the system can answer 'why did it say I was wrong?'; Whisper's word-level timestamps let each graded span (or voice note) be traced back to its audio moment.

Per EDPB Guidelines 02/2021 on Virtual Voice Assistants [FACT — via search snippets attributed to EDPB], voice is personal data and becomes special-category biometric data only when processed to UNIQUELY IDENTIFY a person (speaker-ID, voice embeddings, identity diarization); plain transcription without an identification purpose does not by itself trigger Article 9 — so the system must never run speaker identification.

The recommendation [ESTIMATE — design] to default transcription to local whisper.cpp: zero marginal cost, audio never leaves the machine, and if cloud is chosen later it is exactly one adapter swap behind the seam plus an explicit consent note and the vendor's retention terms.

nodes.definition: Anchor the whole KB to the owner's verbatim brief [FACT — OWNER_BRIEF.md §2a-7]: the learner should not always have to type — e.g. ~10 questions answered by SPEAKING, in WHATEVER LANGUAGE; the answers are SAVED and QUEUED for later analysis by AI, where the local-vs-cloud choice is 'the local AI or the cloud, later on decision' and is therefore explicitly DEFERRED by the owner; voice NOTE-MAKING is also named. The binding consequences are: capture must be spoken and language-agnostic, analysis is deferred/asynchronous, and the architecture must keep BOTH transcription paths open behind one interface because the owner did not pick one. This node fixes what is required so nothing downstream invents a requirement the owner did not state.

included: voice note-making as a named requirement
the owner-DEFERRED local-vs-cloud choice as a binding 'keep both open' constraint

pros.claim: Fixing the owner's exact words stops the pipeline from being over-built for a requirement the owner never stated
pros.example: not selecting cloud STT now because the owner explicitly deferred the local-vs-cloud call

cons.claim: The brief leaves real gaps (exact language set, retention appetite) that must be resolved at build time, not assumed
cons.example: reading 'whatever language' as a promise of uniform accuracy across all 100 Whisper codes

failure_modes: treating the deferred local-vs-cloud decision as already made and hard-coding one path
silently narrowing 'whatever language' to the developer's language
acceptance_tests: the brief is restated with the any-language, saved-and-queued, deferred-transcription and voice-note elements, each tagged FACT to the owner brief, and the deferral is carried as a keep-both-open constraint
revisit_triggers: the owner picks local or cloud
the owner narrows or names the target languages
a new capture modality (photo, handwriting) is added to the brief

base.update_signal: the owner resolves the deferred transcription choice or changes the capture requirement

nodes.definition: Establish the record-now / analyse-later posture as the correct architecture for the brief [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4]: 'saved and queued for later analysis' implies an asynchronous pipeline, which is the cheap and robust choice because no real-time ASR is needed. Capture returns immediately after writing the file and a queued row; the slow work (transcription, grading) runs in a nightly batch aligned with the owner's every-night analysis mode. This posture removes latency pressure from the transcription-engine choice (so even CPU-only local models are fine) and makes the queue, not a live socket, the backbone of the system.

included: the nightly-batch alignment with the owner's analysis mode
excluded: the concrete queue schema (its own node)

pros.claim: Removing the real-time constraint makes the cheapest local model adequate and the whole system simpler
pros.example: running whisper.cpp medium overnight on CPU instead of provisioning a low-latency GPU or paying per-minute cloud STT

cons.claim: Overnight latency means feedback is next-morning, not instant, which can feel slow for a learner wanting immediate correction
cons.example: a learner who speaks 10 answers and expects a score in seconds gets it the next day

failure_modes: over-engineering a real-time ASR path the brief never asked for
coupling capture to analysis so a slow transcription blocks the record UI
acceptance_tests: the design states the async record→queue→nightly-analyse shape, justifies no-real-time-ASR from the brief, and tags itself ESTIMATE-design
revisit_triggers: the owner asks for instant/live feedback
answer volume grows beyond what a nightly batch can clear
a use case needs mid-session transcription

base.update_signal: a latency/interactivity requirement or a volume spike changes the batch posture

nodes.definition: Define the single seam that honours the owner's deferral: a TranscriberInterface with two interchangeable implementations — LocalWhisper (whisper.cpp / faster-whisper) and CloudSTT (a cloud STT API) — so choosing local vs cloud is a config flag, not a rewrite [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4 step 3]. The interface takes an audio file and returns {transcript, detected_language, language_confidence, word_timestamps?}; both sides must satisfy the same contract so the batch worker, grader and audit linkage are engine-agnostic. This is the architectural expression of 'the local AI or the cloud, later on decision' and is the node that keeps the deferred choice genuinely open.

included: the abstract interface and its return contract
LocalWhisper and CloudSTT as the two implementations
excluded: the internals of each implementation (their own nodes)

pros.claim: A stable seam lets the deferred decision be made later by config without touching the worker, grader or storage
pros.example: flipping TRANSCRIBER=cloud in config to A/B a cloud engine without editing the grading path

cons.claim: A lowest-common-denominator interface can hide engine-specific features (e.g. word timestamps, diarization) unless the contract is designed for them
cons.example: an interface that returns only text loses Whisper word timestamps that audit linkage needs

failure_modes: leaking one engine's quirks into the interface so the other cannot satisfy it
defining the contract so thin it drops metadata (language confidence, timestamps) the pipeline needs
acceptance_tests: the interface names both LocalWhisper and CloudSTT, specifies a return contract including detected language + confidence, and demonstrates the choice is a config flag
revisit_triggers: a new transcription engine or modality must plug in
a needed field (timestamps, per-word confidence) is missing from the contract
the owner selects a path and the unused implementation is deprioritised

base.update_signal: a new engine, a missing contract field, or the owner's resolved choice changes the seam

nodes.definition: Specify the capture step: record one audio file per spoken answer, storing lossless-enough compressed audio at 16 kHz mono — which is exactly what Whisper consumes anyway, so no resampling loss is introduced [FACT — Whisper input format; ESTIMATE — the one-file-per-answer choice is design]. Capture is deliberately dumb and fast: it writes the file and hands off to storage/enqueue, doing no transcription itself (that is the async posture). One-file-per-answer keeps the {answer_id ↔ audio} mapping trivial and makes per-question grading and audit linkage clean.

included: one 16 kHz mono file per answer
excluded: the metadata row and queue (its own node)

pros.claim: Recording at Whisper's native 16 kHz mono avoids a resample step and keeps files small
pros.example: a 30-second answer stored as a small 16 kHz mono clip that the worker feeds directly to whisper.cpp

cons.claim: 16 kHz mono discards audio fidelity a future delivery/pronunciation scorer might want
cons.example: a later fluency scorer wishing it had higher-rate stereo audio it can no longer recover

failure_modes: doing transcription inline and blocking the capture UI
batching multiple answers into one file and losing the per-question boundary
acceptance_tests: capture produces one 16 kHz mono file per answer, does no inline transcription, and preserves a clean answer_id↔audio mapping
revisit_triggers: a delivery/pronunciation scorer needs higher-fidelity audio
a device cannot record 16 kHz mono natively
answers must be segmented from a single continuous recording

base.update_signal: a delivery-scoring or device-capability change alters the capture format

nodes.definition: Specify durable storage + enqueue [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4 step 2]: write the audio file to a directory and insert a metadata row {answer_id, question_id, session_id, recorded_at, duration, language_hint?, status:queued} into a SQLite table. A directory-of-files plus one SQLite table is fully sufficient at single-user scale and a message broker (Kafka/RabbitMQ/SQS) would be overkill. The row is the unit of work the nightly worker drains; the file path lives on the row so audio, transcript and grade can later be linked. This is the durability boundary: once the row is committed as queued, the answer cannot be silently lost.

included: the exact row fields and status:queued
excluded: the status transitions themselves (queue state machine node)
the transcription that consumes the row

pros.claim: SQLite + a files directory gives durability, queryability and zero operational overhead at single-user scale
pros.example: one .sqlite file and a folder of clips that back up by copying, no broker to run

cons.claim: SQLite's single-writer model would bottleneck a multi-user or high-concurrency system, so the choice is scale-bounded
cons.example: many simultaneous writers contending on the SQLite lock if the system ever went multi-user

failure_modes: writing the file but failing to commit the row (or vice-versa) so audio and queue diverge
reaching for a message broker the single-user scale does not warrant
acceptance_tests: storage writes the file plus a queued metadata row with the specified fields in SQLite, and the design argues a broker is unnecessary at single-user scale
revisit_triggers: the system goes multi-user or multi-writer
row and file consistency drifts under crash testing
a field (e.g. rubric_id, device) is needed on the row

base.update_signal: a scale change or a row/file consistency failure revises the storage choice

nodes.definition: Define the status lifecycle on each answer row [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4 step 6]: queued → transcribed → graded, with any stage error moving the row to failed(reason). The invariant is that nothing is silently dropped — every answer is in exactly one known state, failures carry a reason, and the nightly worker only ever acts on well-defined transitions. This state machine is what makes the pipeline debuggable and idempotent: a re-run picks up rows by status, and a crash mid-stage leaves a recoverable state rather than a lost answer.

pros.claim: Explicit statuses make the pipeline idempotent and debuggable — every answer is in exactly one known state
pros.example: restarting the worker after a crash and having it resume from status without re-grading finished rows

cons.claim: A too-coarse state set hides where an answer actually failed (transcription vs grading) unless failed(reason) is specific
cons.example: a bare 'failed' status that cannot distinguish an STT error from a grader timeout

failure_modes: leaving an answer in an ambiguous or no state after a crash
collapsing transcription and grading failures into one indistinct status
acceptance_tests: the lifecycle enumerates queued/transcribed/graded/failed(reason), guarantees no silent drop, and supports status-driven idempotent re-runs
revisit_triggers: a new stage (e.g. delivery-scoring) is added to the pipeline
failures cannot be diagnosed from the recorded reason
idempotency breaks under concurrent workers

base.update_signal: a new pipeline stage or a diagnosability gap revises the state machine

nodes.definition: Specify the LocalWhisper implementation behind the seam. whisper.cpp is a dependency-free C/C++ Whisper port running on macOS/iOS/Android/Linux/Windows/Raspberry Pi/WASM with NEON/Metal/CUDA/Vulkan acceleration, quantization and word timestamps [FACT — fetched github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp]; its memory/disk table shows the large model at 2.9 GiB disk / ~3.9 GB RAM, so the full-quality multilingual model runs in under 4 GB RAM on CPU [FACT — fetched table]. faster-whisper reimplements Whisper on CTranslate2 and claims up to 4× faster at the same accuracy with less memory [FACT — fetched github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper]. Because the nightly batch has no latency constraint, CPU-only whisper.cpp medium/large is sufficient; use faster-whisper if an NVIDIA GPU is present [ESTIMATE — design].

included: whisper.cpp and faster-whisper as the local engines
the RAM/disk feasibility (large <4 GB RAM on CPU) [FACT]
excluded: the privacy/retention argument for defaulting local

pros.claim: A local engine runs the full multilingual model at zero marginal cost with audio never leaving the machine
pros.example: whisper.cpp large transcribing overnight on a normal laptop in <4 GB RAM

cons.claim: Local accuracy/speed on weak hardware can trail cloud, and CPU large-model runs are slow per file
cons.example: a low-end machine taking many minutes per answer on the large model overnight

failure_modes: provisioning GPU infrastructure the batch does not need
picking a model too large for the target device's RAM
acceptance_tests: the local path names whisper.cpp/faster-whisper, cites the <4 GB-RAM large-model feasibility as FACT, and states CPU-only batch suffices with GPU as optional
revisit_triggers: target-device RAM/CPU changes the feasible model size
a new Whisper model version (e.g. large-v3) shifts accuracy/coverage
batch runtime per file becomes unacceptable

base.update_signal: a device-capability or Whisper-model-version change updates the local path

nodes.definition: Specify the CloudSTT implementation behind the seam. Existent, commonly-used cloud STT APIs: Google Cloud Speech-to-Text (vendor claim 125+ languages) [FACT — via search snippet, vendor claim], Microsoft Azure AI Speech (large locale table; exact current count [UNKNOWN] — page not fetchable), Amazon Transcribe (supported-languages page exists; a blog documented 31 languages as of its date; current count [UNKNOWN]), and the OpenAI Audio API (whisper-1 plus the gpt-4o-transcribe family; whisper-1 has a 25 MB per-file upload limit; help center lists ~57 officially supported transcription languages) [FACT — via search snippet; direct fetch 403]. Deepgram and AssemblyAI are also well-known specialist vendors, but no numbers are claimed for them [ESTIMATE — not fetched]. Cloud buys coverage/scale at the cost of sending audio off-device.

included: Google/Azure/Amazon/OpenAI as the cloud options with their honesty-tagged coverage
excluded: the privacy law analysis (its own node)
the vendor retention terms (its own node)

pros.claim: Cloud STT offers broad claimed language coverage and offloads compute from the device
pros.example: Google's claimed 125+ languages exceeding the local Whisper 100-code table on paper

cons.claim: Cloud requires sending audio off-device and its exact per-vendor language counts are UNKNOWN without a live fetch
cons.example: quoting Azure's or Amazon's current supported-language count when the pages were not fetchable

failure_modes: stating a vendor's current language count as fact when only a stale or snippet figure exists
ignoring per-file upload limits (whisper-1 25 MB) for long answers
acceptance_tests: the cloud path lists the four providers with FACT/UNKNOWN-tagged coverage, notes the whisper-1 25 MB limit, and flags that off-device audio raises the privacy question
revisit_triggers: a vendor's supported-language page becomes fetchable and counts can be confirmed
a per-file size or pricing limit changes
the owner selects cloud and a specific vendor must be pinned

base.update_signal: a vendor page becomes fetchable or a limit/price changes the cloud path

nodes.definition: Resolve the owner's 'whatever language' requirement honestly. Whisper's LANGUAGES dict contains exactly 100 entries (the '~99' figure predates Cantonese/yue in large-v3) [FACT — fetched and machine-counted from openai/whisper tokenizer.py]; multilingual recognition, speech translation and language identification are core features and accuracy varies strongly by language, with per-language WER breakdowns published for large-v2/v3 [FACT — fetched]. Practically, Whisper's language-identification handles 'whatever language' WITHOUT asking the learner to declare one, and the pipeline stores the detected language with its confidence on the row. The honest posture: 100 codes is the local coverage ceiling and a low-resource language may transcribe poorly, so detected-language confidence should gate whether a transcript is trusted for grading.

included: storing detected language + confidence and the per-language accuracy caveat
excluded: the grading that consumes the transcript

pros.claim: Language-identification meets 'any language' without a UI language picker and records confidence for downstream trust
pros.example: a learner speaking Hindi then Spanish, each auto-detected and stored with confidence, no picker shown

cons.claim: Coverage is not uniform accuracy — a low-resource language within the 100 can transcribe badly and mislead the grader
cons.example: a high word-error transcript in a low-resource language producing a wrong rubric grade

failure_modes: reading '100 languages' as '100 languages at equal accuracy'
grading a low-confidence transcript as if it were reliable
acceptance_tests: the coverage is stated as exactly 100 Whisper codes [FACT], LID removes the declare step, detected-language+confidence is stored, and per-language accuracy variance gates trust
revisit_triggers: a new Whisper model changes the language set or per-language WER
the owner names a low-resource target language
confidence-gating thresholds need tuning from real transcripts

base.update_signal: a Whisper-model language-set change or a named low-resource language updates coverage

nodes.definition: Define the nightly batch-transcribe worker [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4 step 3]: aligned with the owner's every-night analysis mode, it selects rows with status=queued, runs each audio file through the TranscriberInterface (whichever implementation the config flag selects), and writes back the transcript plus the detected language and confidence, advancing the row to status=transcribed. Because the batch is overnight there is no latency constraint, so a CPU-only local model is adequate. The worker is engine-agnostic by construction (it only knows the interface), idempotent (it acts by status), and the join point where capture, transcription and the state machine meet.

included: writing transcript + detected language + confidence and advancing to transcribed

pros.claim: An engine-agnostic, status-driven worker cleanly separates 'what to transcribe' from 'which engine', honouring the seam
pros.example: the same worker running local one night and cloud the next by config, with no code change

cons.claim: A single nightly pass means a large backlog can exceed the window and spill to the next night
cons.example: a burst of long answers that the CPU model cannot clear before morning

failure_modes: hard-coding an engine instead of calling the interface
not persisting detected language/confidence so downstream trust-gating is impossible
acceptance_tests: the worker drains status=queued through the interface, persists transcript+detected-language+confidence, advances status to transcribed, and is idempotent by status
revisit_triggers: nightly backlog exceeds the window
the interface contract gains a field the worker must persist
a per-file failure pattern needs mid-batch handling

base.update_signal: a backlog overrun or an interface-contract change revises the worker

nodes.definition: Define the grading step [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4 step 4]: feed the transcript plus the question's model answer / rubric to an LLM grader that returns {score, per-rubric-dimension subscores, error notes, misconception tags}, then advance the row to status=graded. The grader scores the CONTENT of the answer from the transcript (delivery is handled separately). Structured output (a fixed schema of subscores + tags) is what makes the grade consumable by the learner model. This is the highest-value and highest-risk step: a wrong grade corrupts the learner model, so grades must be schema-validated and traceable back to the transcript that produced them.

included: transcript + rubric → {score, subscores, error notes, misconception tags}
structured output that the learner model can consume
excluded: the SpeechRater precedent grounding (its own node)
the content-vs-delivery carve-out detail (its own node)

pros.claim: A structured per-dimension grade turns a free-form spoken answer into learner-model signal automatically
pros.example: a transcript scored into {content:3/4, completeness:2/4, misconception:['confuses X with Y']} the scheduler can act on

cons.claim: The grade is only as good as the transcript and the rubric, and an LLM can hallucinate a subscore or misread a garbled transcript
cons.example: a low-confidence transcript graded confidently, injecting a wrong mastery update

failure_modes: grading a low-confidence/garbled transcript as if reliable
emitting unstructured prose the learner model cannot parse
acceptance_tests: the grader consumes transcript + rubric, emits a schema-validated {score, subscores, error notes, misconception tags}, grades content by default, and advances status to graded
revisit_triggers: rubric dimensions change for a course
grader agreement with human scores drifts
transcript-confidence gating for grading needs tuning

base.update_signal: a rubric change or a grader-vs-human agreement drift revises the grading step

nodes.definition: Ground the automated-grading claim in established practice. ETS — the maker of TOEFL — has operated SpeechRater, an automated scoring engine for spontaneous non-native speech, since ~2008 (ETS Research Reports on SpeechRater v1.0 in 2008 and the v5.0 engine in 2018) [FACT — via search snippets; ets.org direct fetch 403]. Operational TOEFL iBT Speaking is scored by a COMBINATION of human raters (holistic: content/meaning/language) and SpeechRater (analytic: delivery/language-use features) [FACT — via search snippets], with the exact current human/machine weighting [UNKNOWN — official ETS scoring page not fetchable]. The implication: LLM-grading of transcribed spoken answers against a rubric is not exotic — the very exam this system targets already machine-scores speech — which de-risks the grading design as precedented, not novel.

included: the exact weighting [UNKNOWN] and the 'not exotic' implication
excluded: the internal SpeechRater feature set beyond delivery/language-use

pros.claim: A named operational precedent (SpeechRater since ~2008) shows automated spoken-answer scoring is normal, de-risking the design
pros.example: citing that TOEFL itself machine-scores speaking when justifying the LLM grader to a skeptic

cons.claim: SpeechRater scores delivery features analytically alongside humans, so it is not a like-for-like precedent for a pure-content LLM grader
cons.example: over-claiming that SpeechRater validates content-only LLM grading when it actually scores delivery and pairs with human raters

failure_modes: stating the exact human/machine weighting as fact when it is UNKNOWN
over-generalizing a delivery-scoring precedent to justify content-only grading
acceptance_tests: the precedent names SpeechRater since ~2008 and the TOEFL human+machine combination as FACT, holds the exact weighting UNKNOWN, and draws the 'automated spoken grading is precedented' conclusion
revisit_triggers: the official ETS scoring page becomes fetchable and the weighting is confirmed
a newer SpeechRater engine version is published
the target exam is not TOEFL and a different precedent is needed

base.update_signal: a fetchable ETS scoring page or a new SpeechRater version updates the precedent

nodes.definition: Draw the scoring boundary [ESTIMATE — design consequence, research §B5]: grade the CONTENT from the transcript and do NOT grade pronunciation/delivery unless the course is TOEFL-speaking, where delivery is part of the construct. Delivery features (fluency, pause patterns, rhythm) live in the AUDIO, not the transcript, so for a delivery-scoring future step the audio path must stay available (it does, via storage + audit linkage). This node prevents two errors: penalizing a correct answer for a non-native accent when only content matters, and conversely ignoring delivery when the exam explicitly scores it. The default is content-only; delivery is an opt-in per course.

included: keeping the audio path available for a future delivery scorer
excluded: the actual delivery-feature extraction (out of scope, future)
the rubric dimensions of content grading

pros.claim: Separating content from delivery avoids penalizing a correct answer for accent while still allowing delivery scoring where the exam requires it
pros.example: a chemistry answer graded on correctness regardless of accent, but a TOEFL-speaking answer also scored on fluency

cons.claim: Deferring delivery scoring means the transcript-only grade misses fluency/pause signal some courses care about until the audio step is built
cons.example: a speaking-practice user getting only content feedback while delivery feedback waits on a future step

failure_modes: grading pronunciation for a course that only cares about content
discarding audio and foreclosing a future delivery scorer
acceptance_tests: the boundary sets content-only grading by default, carves out TOEFL-speaking for delivery, and confirms the audio path stays available for a future delivery step
revisit_triggers: a course adds delivery to its construct
a delivery-feature extractor is built
learners request pronunciation feedback

base.update_signal: a course adding delivery scoring or a delivery extractor being built revises the boundary

nodes.definition: Define the write-back step [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4 step 5]: the grading output updates the per-item mastery state and the weakness map in the learner model, which the scheduler consumes the next morning to choose what to review. A key discipline carried from the research: the day-view EFFORT metric and the course-view MASTERY metric are different and must not be conflated — this write-back feeds mastery, not effort. The write-back is the point where a spoken answer finally becomes learning signal; it must be transactional with the graded status so a partial write cannot leave the learner model inconsistent with the queue.

included: not conflating effort (day view) with mastery (course view)
excluded: the audit linkage that makes it explainable

pros.claim: Writing grades into the mastery/weakness model closes the loop so speaking practice actually drives the next day's review
pros.example: a misconception tag from a spoken answer surfacing the related item in tomorrow's queue

cons.claim: A wrong grade propagates into the learner model and mis-schedules review, so the write-back amplifies grading errors
cons.example: a hallucinated low subscore demoting an item the learner actually knows

failure_modes: conflating effort and mastery metrics in the write-back
a non-transactional write leaving the learner model inconsistent with the graded status
acceptance_tests: the write-back updates per-item mastery + weakness map for the next-morning scheduler, keeps effort and mastery distinct, and is transactional with the graded status
revisit_triggers: the learner-model schema changes
grading error rate makes write-back amplification material
the scheduler needs a new field from the grade

base.update_signal: a learner-model schema change or a grading-error-amplification signal revises the write-back

nodes.definition: Define audit linkage [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4 step 5 / §B6]: keep audio + transcript + grade linked so the system can answer 'why did it say I was wrong?'. Whisper's word-level timestamps let each graded span — or each voice-note fragment — be traced back to its exact audio moment. Concretely, the graded row references the transcript, which references the audio file and its timestamps; nothing is discarded after grading. This is what makes the grade contestable and debuggable by the learner and the developer, and it is also the mechanism a future delivery-scoring step would reuse to locate fluency features in the audio.

included: Whisper word timestamps for moment-level traceback
keeping artifacts for contestability and a future delivery step

pros.claim: Linked artifacts make every grade explainable and contestable, building learner trust
pros.example: a learner tapping a low subscore and hearing the exact audio span and reading the transcript that produced it

cons.claim: Retaining audio + transcript + grade increases the stored personal-data footprint that privacy rules then govern
cons.example: keeping raw voice recordings indefinitely enlarging the data a breach would expose

failure_modes: discarding audio or transcript after grading so a grade cannot be explained
losing the timestamp linkage so a graded span cannot be located in the audio
acceptance_tests: the linkage keeps audio↔transcript↔grade joined with word timestamps, supports answering 'why was I marked wrong', and is reusable by a future delivery step
revisit_triggers: a retention policy caps how long audio is kept
the learner-model or transcript schema breaks the linkage
a delivery scorer needs the timestamp path

base.update_signal: a retention cap or a schema change affecting the linkage revises audit linkage

nodes.definition: Define failure handling [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4 step 6]: any stage error moves the row to failed(reason) rather than losing it; failed items are retried on the next nightly run, and nothing is silently dropped. The reason string distinguishes transcription failures (bad audio, unsupported/low-confidence language) from grading failures (LLM error, malformed rubric) so retries can be targeted and persistent failures surfaced rather than looping forever. This node is the operational safety net over the queue state machine: it turns transient errors into recoverable work and makes chronic failures visible for human attention.

included: surfacing chronic failures instead of infinite retry
excluded: the specific error taxonomy per engine

pros.claim: Retrying failed rows next night with a captured reason means transient errors self-heal and nothing is lost
pros.example: a row that failed on a corrupt audio read succeeding on the next night's retry after the file is re-fetched

cons.claim: Naive infinite retry can loop forever on a permanently bad item, so a give-up/surface threshold is needed
cons.example: an unrecoverably corrupt file retried every night without ever being flagged for a human

failure_modes: retrying a permanently failing item forever with no escalation
collapsing distinct failure reasons so retries cannot be targeted
acceptance_tests: failures move to failed(reason), retry next night, distinguish transcription vs grading causes, and escalate chronic failures rather than looping forever
revisit_triggers: a retry storm or infinite-loop pattern appears
a new failure mode needs its own reason code
an escalation/alerting path is added

base.update_signal: a retry-storm pattern or a new failure mode revises the handling policy

nodes.definition: Establish the privacy constraint for cloud (and stored) audio. Per the EDPB Guidelines 02/2021 on Virtual Voice Assistants, voice data is inherently personal data and becomes Article 9 SPECIAL-CATEGORY biometric data specifically when it is processed to UNIQUELY IDENTIFY a person (speaker-ID, voice embeddings, identity diarization); plain transcription without an identification purpose does not by itself trigger Article 9 [FACT — via search snippets attributed to EDPB]. The binding design consequence: NEVER run speaker identification on the recordings — a single-user study system has no need to, and doing so would pull the data into the far stricter Article 9 regime [last clause ESTIMATE — design]. This keeps the system on the plain-transcription side of the biometric threshold.

included: EDPB Guidelines 02/2021: voice personal; Article 9 only when processed to identify [FACT]
staying on the plain-transcription side of the biometric threshold
excluded: the vendor retention terms (its own node)
non-EU regimes not covered by the research

pros.claim: Refusing speaker-ID keeps the system on the plain-transcription side of the Article 9 biometric threshold, avoiding special-category obligations
pros.example: transcribing answers for content without ever computing a voice embedding that would identify the speaker

cons.claim: The analysis is grounded in EU EDPB guidance via search snippets, so a non-EU jurisdiction or a direct-fetch confirmation may shift the specifics
cons.example: assuming EU biometric rules govern a US-based user without checking the applicable regime

failure_modes: adding speaker identification/diarization-for-identity and crossing into Article 9
treating stored voice as non-personal data
acceptance_tests: the constraint cites EDPB Guidelines 02/2021 with the identify-to-become-biometric distinction as FACT and mandates never running speaker identification
revisit_triggers: the EDPB guidelines page becomes directly fetchable for confirmation
a feature proposing voice-ID/diarization is requested
a non-EU jurisdiction's rules must be checked

base.update_signal: a fetchable EDPB confirmation or a voice-ID feature request revises the privacy constraint

nodes.definition: Capture the vendor data-use terms that a cloud choice must weigh. OpenAI's API policy states that API inputs/outputs are NOT used for model training by default (since 2023-03-01, opt-in only), may be retained up to 30 days for abuse monitoring, and that zero-data-retention is available for qualifying orgs [FACT — via search snippets attributed to openai.com]. Other major clouds publish comparable data-use terms, but their specific current terms are [UNKNOWN — not fetched this session; verify the chosen vendor's page at decision time]. The honest posture: only the OpenAI terms are citable here at snippet grade, and any cloud selection must re-verify the actual vendor's live retention page before audio is sent.

pros.claim: Knowing the default data-use posture lets the cloud path be chosen without accidentally opting into training on learner audio
pros.example: relying on OpenAI's not-trained-by-default term while budgeting for ≤30-day retention

cons.claim: Only OpenAI's terms are citable at snippet grade; assuming other vendors match is unverified
cons.example: quoting a competitor cloud's retention window that was never fetched

failure_modes: assuming all clouds share OpenAI's terms
sending audio before verifying the chosen vendor's live retention page
acceptance_tests: the terms cite OpenAI's not-trained-by-default/≤30-day/ZDR posture as FACT-snippet, hold other vendors UNKNOWN, and require re-verifying the live page before sending audio
revisit_triggers: a specific cloud vendor is selected and its live terms are fetched
a vendor changes its data-use policy
an enterprise ZDR agreement is negotiated

base.update_signal: a selected vendor's live terms or a policy change updates the retention picture

nodes.definition: State the default posture given the owner deferred the choice [ESTIMATE — recommendation, research §B7]: default transcription to LOCAL whisper.cpp — it covers the need at zero marginal cost and the audio never leaves the machine, side-stepping both the EDPB biometric question and the vendor-retention question for the common case. If cloud is chosen later, that is exactly ONE adapter swap behind the transcriber seam (flip the config flag) PLUS recording an explicit consent note and the vendor's retention terms. This node ties the seam, the privacy constraint and the retention terms into a single default the owner can accept now without foreclosing the deferred cloud option.

included: default-to-local at zero marginal cost, audio stays on device
cloud-later = one adapter swap + consent note + retention terms
reconciling the seam, privacy and retention into one default
excluded: the concrete local model selection (local impl node)

pros.claim: Defaulting local resolves the deferred choice safely now while keeping cloud a one-flag swap later
pros.example: shipping on whisper.cpp with audio never leaving the device, and enabling cloud later by config plus a consent note

cons.claim: A local default may under-serve a language or device where cloud accuracy/scale would be materially better
cons.example: a low-resource language that a cloud engine transcribes far better than the local model

failure_modes: treating the local default as a permanent decision that forecloses the owner's deferred cloud option
switching to cloud without recording consent and retention terms
acceptance_tests: the recommendation defaults to local (zero cost, on-device), keeps cloud as one adapter swap plus consent + retention terms, and does not foreclose the deferred choice
revisit_triggers: the owner selects cloud
a language/device makes cloud materially better
a consent/retention policy is finalized

base.update_signal: the owner's resolved choice or a language/device advantage revises the default

nodes.definition: Model the owner's named voice NOTE-MAKING requirement as a reuse of the same pipeline minus grading [ESTIMATE — design, research §B6]: record → transcribe → LLM post-process (clean up, punctuate, structure into note/flashcard candidates per the flashcard-quality rules) → HUMAN-CONFIRM before anything enters the KB. Whisper's word timestamps let each note fragment link back to its audio moment (shared audit linkage). The critical difference from grading is the human-confirm gate: notes become durable knowledge only after the learner approves them, so the LLM proposes and the human disposes, preventing hallucinated notes from polluting the KB.

pros.claim: Reusing the capture/transcribe pipeline for notes adds voice note-making at almost no extra architecture
pros.example: the same record+transcribe path feeding an LLM cleanup step that proposes flashcard candidates

cons.claim: Without the human-confirm gate an LLM could inject hallucinated or malformed notes into the KB
cons.example: an auto-generated flashcard with a wrong fact entering the review deck unreviewed

failure_modes: auto-committing LLM-structured notes to the KB without human confirmation
grading voice notes as if they were exam answers
acceptance_tests: the note path reuses record→transcribe→LLM-post-process→human-confirm, structures note/flashcard candidates, and gates KB entry on human confirmation
revisit_triggers: the flashcard-quality rules change
notes volume warrants batching alongside grading
a confirm-UI change alters the human gate

base.update_signal: a flashcard-rule change or a notes-volume shift revises the voice-note path

nodes.definition: Compose the whole capture→grade→write-back pipeline into a defensible go/no-go verdict [ESTIMATE — design synthesis]. Each stage carries a binding gate: capture+storage must be durable (row committed, no silent loss); the queue state machine must keep every answer in a known state; transcription must meet the language-coverage/confidence bar; grading must be schema-valid and grounded in the SpeechRater precedent; write-back must be transactional and auditable; and the privacy posture must default local with cloud gated on consent+retention. The verdict is GO only when every stage gate holds; a failing gate localizes the no-go to a stage rather than condemning the whole design. This node exists so the pipeline is shipped as a checklist of passed gates, not an act of faith.

included: the per-stage gate list and the all-gates-hold GO rule
localizing a no-go to a failing stage
shipping as a checklist of passed gates
excluded: the internals of each gated stage (their own nodes)

pros.claim: A per-stage gate checklist makes the ship/no-ship call auditable and localizes any failure to one stage
pros.example: a no-go pinned to 'transcription confidence gate failing on low-resource language' rather than rejecting the whole pipeline

cons.claim: Composed gates are only as honest as each stage's own acceptance test, so a weak per-stage gate hides risk in the verdict
cons.example: a green verdict masking an untested grading gate that later corrupts the learner model

failure_modes: declaring GO while a stage gate is untested or failing
condemning the whole pipeline for a single localizable stage failure
acceptance_tests: the verdict enumerates each stage gate, sets GO only when all hold, and localizes a no-go to the specific failing stage
revisit_triggers: any upstream stage's gate definition changes
a real deployment surfaces a gate the checklist missed
the owner resolves the deferred cloud choice and its gate changes

base.update_signal: an upstream gate change or a missed-gate deployment finding revises the verdict

conflict_axes.name: local_vs_cloud_transcription
conflict_axes.description: Local whisper.cpp gives zero marginal cost and on-device privacy; cloud STT gives broader claimed coverage and offloaded compute at the cost of sending audio off-device.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default local behind the seam; switch to cloud only when a language/device makes it materially better, gated on consent + retention

conflict_axes.name: batch_nightly_vs_realtime_feedback
conflict_axes.description: The async nightly batch is cheap and robust but delays feedback to next morning, while a learner may want an instant score.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the durable nightly batch as the backbone and add a real-time path behind the seam only if instant feedback is later required

conflict_axes.name: content_grading_vs_delivery_grading
conflict_axes.description: Grading content from the transcript avoids penalizing accent, but some exams (TOEFL-speaking) score delivery which lives in the audio, not the transcript.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: content-only by default, delivery scoring opt-in per course whose construct includes it, keeping the audio path available

conflict_axes.name: coverage_breadth_vs_per_language_accuracy
conflict_axes.description: Whisper's 100-code table is broad coverage, but accuracy varies strongly by language so breadth is not uniform reliability.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: store detected-language confidence and gate whether a transcript is trusted for grading rather than assuming equal accuracy

conflict_axes.name: sqlite_simplicity_vs_scaling_headroom
conflict_axes.description: A directory-of-files plus one SQLite table is ideal at single-user scale but its single-writer model would bottleneck a multi-user system.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep SQLite+files while single-user and only revisit if the system genuinely goes multi-writer

conflict_axes.name: speaker_id_convenience_vs_biometric_privacy
conflict_axes.description: Speaker identification could add features but pulls the data into the stricter Article 9 special-category biometric regime.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never run speaker identification on a single-user system so the data stays plain transcription below the Article 9 threshold

conflict_axes.name: automated_grade_vs_human_rater_trust
conflict_axes.description: Fully automated LLM grading scales but the SpeechRater precedent pairs machine scoring with human raters, raising how much to trust a machine-only grade.
poles: keep a human in the loop
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ship automated grading grounded in the SpeechRater precedent but keep grades auditable and contestable so a human can override

conflict_axes.name: retry_forever_vs_surface_chronic_failure
conflict_axes.description: Retrying failed items next night self-heals transient errors but naive infinite retry loops forever on a permanently bad item.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: retry transient failures with a captured reason but escalate chronic failures to human attention after a threshold

conflict_axes.name: resolve_now_vs_keep_deferred_open
conflict_axes.description: Picking local or cloud now would simplify the build, but the owner explicitly deferred and wants both paths kept open.
poles: keep both open behind the seam
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: honour the deferral with the interface seam and a reversible local default rather than hard-coding a choice the owner postponed

edge_cases.description: A learner speaks a low-resource language that Whisper transcribes with high word-error, and the grader scores the garbled transcript confidently
edge_cases.trigger: a low-confidence transcript is passed to grading as if reliable
edge_cases.mitigation: store detected-language confidence and gate grading on it, flagging low-confidence transcripts for review instead of grading them

edge_cases.description: The audio file is written but the SQLite row is not committed (or vice-versa), so audio and queue diverge
edge_cases.trigger: a crash between the file write and the row insert
edge_cases.mitigation: commit the file and the queued row atomically (or reconcile orphaned files/rows on startup) so no answer is half-stored

edge_cases.description: An answer is left in an ambiguous or no state after a mid-stage crash and is silently lost
edge_cases.trigger: the worker dies between reading a row and updating its status
edge_cases.mitigation: make transitions idempotent and status-driven so a re-run resumes the row from its last known state, never dropping it

edge_cases.description: A permanently corrupt audio file is retried every night forever without ever being surfaced
edge_cases.trigger: a naive infinite-retry policy with no give-up threshold
edge_cases.mitigation: cap retries and escalate chronic failures to human attention with the captured reason rather than looping

edge_cases.description: The LLM grader hallucinates a subscore or misreads a garbled transcript, and the wrong grade is written into the learner model
edge_cases.trigger: an unvalidated or low-confidence grade is applied to mastery
edge_cases.mitigation: schema-validate the grade, gate write-back on transcript confidence, and keep the grade auditable so it can be contested and reversed

edge_cases.description: A whisper-1 cloud call rejects a long answer that exceeds the 25 MB per-file upload limit
edge_cases.trigger: an answer audio file larger than the vendor per-file cap is sent to the cloud engine
edge_cases.mitigation: keep 16 kHz mono compact capture and chunk or reject over-limit files before the cloud call

edge_cases.description: Speaker identification or diarization-for-identity is added and pulls the voice data into the Article 9 special-category regime
edge_cases.trigger: a voice-ID or identity-diarization feature is proposed for a single-user system that does not need it
edge_cases.mitigation: never run speaker identification; keep processing to plain transcription so the data stays below the Article 9 biometric threshold

edge_cases.description: The system is quoted a specific cloud vendor's current language count or retention window that was never actually fetched
edge_cases.trigger: an UNKNOWN vendor figure is stated as fact from memory or a stale snippet
edge_cases.mitigation: hold non-fetched vendor counts/terms as UNKNOWN and re-verify the live vendor page before selection or before sending audio

edge_cases.description: The nightly backlog of long answers exceeds the batch window and spills unprocessed into the next night
edge_cases.trigger: a burst of answers the CPU model cannot clear before morning
edge_cases.mitigation: prioritize by age/status, allow the batch to resume by status next night, and use faster-whisper/GPU or a smaller model if the window is chronically overrun

edge_cases.description: An LLM-structured voice note with a wrong fact is auto-committed to the KB without human confirmation
edge_cases.trigger: the human-confirm gate is skipped for voice-note post-processing
edge_cases.mitigation: require human confirmation before any note/flashcard candidate enters the KB, so the LLM proposes and the human disposes

edge_cases.description: Audio or transcript is discarded after grading, so a learner's 'why was I marked wrong?' cannot be answered
edge_cases.trigger: artifacts are deleted at grading time with no retention for audit
edge_cases.mitigation: keep audio↔transcript↔grade linked with word timestamps until a retention policy deliberately expires them

edge_cases.description: The content grader penalizes a correct answer for a non-native accent on a course that only cares about content
edge_cases.trigger: delivery features leak into a content-only grade
edge_cases.mitigation: grade content-only from the transcript by default and enable delivery scoring solely for courses whose construct includes it

dominance_rules.trigger: a low-confidence transcript reaches the grader
dominance_rules.action: gate grading on detected-language confidence and flag low-confidence transcripts for review instead of grading them

dominance_rules.trigger: delivery features influence a content-only course grade
dominance_rules.action: grade content-only from the transcript and enable delivery scoring only for courses (e.g. TOEFL-speaking) that require it

dominance_rules.rule: The never-run-speaker-ID rule dominates any voice-ID feature
dominance_rules.rationale: speaker identification pulls the data into the Article 9 special-category biometric regime a single-user system does not need
dominance_rules.trigger: a speaker-ID or identity-diarization feature is proposed
dominance_rules.action: refuse speaker identification and keep processing to plain transcription below the Article 9 threshold

dominance_rules.rule: The local default dominates cloud until a concrete reason overrides it
dominance_rules.rationale: local is zero-cost and keeps audio on-device, side-stepping the biometric and retention questions
dominance_rules.trigger: cloud is proposed without a language/device justification
dominance_rules.action: stay on local behind the seam and switch to cloud only with a concrete advantage plus consent and retention terms

dominance_rules.rule: UNKNOWN dominates a convenient fact for unfetched vendor figures
dominance_rules.rationale: vendor language counts and retention windows not fetched this session must not be stated as fact
dominance_rules.trigger: a specific cloud vendor's current count or terms is about to be asserted
dominance_rules.action: hold it UNKNOWN and re-verify the live vendor page before selection or before sending audio

dominance_rules.rule: The human-confirm gate dominates auto-commit for voice notes
dominance_rules.rationale: an LLM can propose a wrong or malformed note that would pollute the KB
dominance_rules.trigger: a note/flashcard candidate is about to enter the KB
dominance_rules.action: require human confirmation so the LLM proposes and the human disposes

dominance_rules.rule: Auditability dominates storage economy after grading
dominance_rules.rationale: a grade that cannot be explained cannot be trusted or contested
dominance_rules.trigger: audio or transcript is about to be discarded at grading time
dominance_rules.action: keep audio↔transcript↔grade linked with timestamps until a retention policy deliberately expires them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Put transcription behind the interface seam before writing the batch worker or grader
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a hard-coded engine that must be torn out when the owner resolves local-vs-cloud

anti_rework_rules.rule: Design the queue status lifecycle and no-silent-drop invariant before coding the worker
anti_rework_rules.prevents: answers lost or stuck in ambiguous states that a later audit cannot recover

anti_rework_rules.rule: Commit the audio file and its queued row atomically from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: audio/queue divergence that has to be reconciled after a crash surfaces orphans

anti_rework_rules.rule: Store detected-language confidence at transcription time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-transcribing later to obtain the confidence needed to gate grading

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep audio↔transcript↔grade linked with word timestamps as artifacts are produced
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding traceability after the fact to answer 'why was I marked wrong?'

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide content-only grading (with the TOEFL-speaking carve-out) before building the grader
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reworking the grader when accent-penalization complaints surface

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the never-run-speaker-ID and local-default posture before enabling any cloud call
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unwinding an Article 9 biometric exposure or an unconsented cloud upload after the fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Add the human-confirm gate to the voice-note path before it can write to the KB
anti_rework_rules.prevents: purging hallucinated auto-committed notes out of the review deck later

iteration_protocol.trigger: the owner resolves the deferred local-vs-cloud transcription choice
iteration_protocol.action: flip the config flag, pin the selected implementation, and record consent + retention terms if cloud

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new Whisper model version changes the language set or per-language WER
iteration_protocol.action: update the coverage ceiling and the confidence-gating thresholds and re-confirm the any-language claim

iteration_protocol.trigger: grader-vs-human agreement drifts or a course changes its rubric dimensions
iteration_protocol.action: re-tune the grading prompt/schema and re-validate against the SpeechRater-style precedent

iteration_protocol.trigger: the nightly backlog chronically exceeds the batch window
iteration_protocol.action: prioritize by age/status and move to faster-whisper/GPU or a smaller model

iteration_protocol.trigger: a specific cloud vendor is selected and its live language/retention pages are fetched
iteration_protocol.action: replace the UNKNOWN vendor figures with confirmed values and re-check the per-file limits

iteration_protocol.trigger: a delivery/pronunciation scorer is requested or a course adds delivery to its construct
iteration_protocol.action: build the audio-path delivery step and update the content-vs-delivery boundary

iteration_protocol.trigger: the EDPB guidelines page becomes directly fetchable or a jurisdiction other than the EU applies
iteration_protocol.action: re-confirm the biometric-threshold analysis and the never-run-speaker-ID rule against the applicable regime

iteration_protocol.trigger: the system moves beyond single-user or a row/file consistency failure appears
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the SQLite+files storage choice and the atomic-commit boundary

priority_rationale: The owner brief, async posture and transcriber seam come first because they fix the binding requirement (spoken, any-language, deferred local-vs-cloud) and the architecture that keeps the deferral open; capture, SQLite store/enqueue and the queue state machine next, because they are the durability backbone every later stage drains; the two transcription implementations and the language-coverage model then make 'any language' real and honestly bounded; the nightly worker, the LLM rubric-grader, the SpeechRater grounding and the content-vs-delivery boundary turn transcripts into precedented, well-scoped grades; the learner-model write-back and audit linkage convert grades into auditable learning signal; failure handling, the privacy/biometric constraint, vendor retention and the local-default recommendation govern robustness and data protection; and the voice-note reuse and the composed go/no-go come last because they extend and then gate the whole pipeline stage by stage.
